slow.what: sustained: +6 ms sleep in forward on every step 80 to 159 (a throttled GPU)
periodic: +20 ms on every 25th step (work only rank 0 does, such as logging or an evaluation)
mild: +2 ms on every step 200 to 300

scen.title: Slurm: one rank crashes (exit 13)
scen.outcome: job FAILED; resubmit resumes from the step-100 checkpoint

scen.title: Slurm + torchrun --max-restarts=2 (default store sharing)
scen.outcome: in-job restart fails to re-form the process group (repeated: job 46 failed the same way)

scen.title: Slurm + torchrun --max-restarts=2, TORCH_DISABLE_SHARE_RDZV_TCP_STORE=1
scen.outcome: restarted inside the job in seconds

scen.title: Slurm + --max-restarts=2: a crash that happens every time
scen.outcome: restarts cannot fix a deterministic bug (or a bad batch): budget spent, job FAILED

scen.title: Slurm: a node container killed (docker kill)
scen.outcome: NODE_FAIL, requeued automatically, resumed on a healthy node

scen.title: Slurm: one rank hangs (SIGSTOP), timeout 30 s
scen.outcome: nothing notices until the collective timeout; the report blames the wrong rank

scen.title: Kubernetes (JobSet, maxRestarts 0): one rank crashes
scen.outcome: JobSet Failed (the running example's spec allows no restart)

scen.title: Kubernetes: a worker node goes silent (docker pause), timeout 30 s
scen.outcome: stuck until a person marks the node out of service

scen.title: Ray: a worker node container killed (docker kill)
scen.outcome: waits for capacity: no spare node, so it resumed only when the node came back

sources.name: Llama 3 405B pre-training
sources.unit: unexpected interruptions of one training job
sources.note: Printed "Faulty GPU 148, 30.1%" is a misprint: 148 / 419 = 35.3%. The text's 58.7% for GPU issues sums the printed GPU-row percentages; by counts 64.0%.

sources.name: Recurring 32K-GPU job
sources.cite: Training LLMs with Fault Tolerant HSDP on 100,000 GPUs, Table 1 (arXiv 2602.00277v1, 30 Jan 2026)
sources.unit: unexpected interruptions of one recurring job
sources.note: Every printed percentage matches its count (678 in all). The successor to Llama 3's table: "'Faulty GPU Compute' used to be the top cause, but is now reduced to the fourth (7.4%) ... HBM issues rose to become the top issue." The paper's "a failure every 18 minutes" at 100K GPUs does not follow from its own 2.3 interruptions per 1,000 servers per day (that gives about one every 50 minutes); 18 minutes matches Meta's RSC-1 rate.

sources.name: All LLM training jobs, three months
sources.note: Percentages match counts (55,365). The text says 38,236 explicit and 5,948 implicit failures; the table sums to 39,687 and 6,096 (the implicit gap is exactly the NaN row). CUDA Error is a symptom: it may hide user bugs. CPU OOM and overload are mapped to user code here (our choice; they can be platform limits).

sources.name: Acme LLM development clusters
sources.cite: Hu et al., Characterization of LLM Development in the Datacenter (NSDI 2024), Table 3 (arXiv 2403.07648v2)
sources.unit: failed jobs; second column: share of the GPU time those failures cost
sources.note: 2,575 failed jobs: script errors are 73.4% of failures but 3.2% of the GPU time lost; infrastructure is 10.9% of failures and 82.1% of the GPU time ("over 82% GPU resources ... 11% failed job quantity", reproduced).

sources.name: Philly multi-tenant GPU clusters
sources.cite: Jeon et al., Analysis of Large-Scale Multi-Tenant GPU Clusters for DNN Training Workloads (USENIX ATC 2019), Table 7
sources.unit: failure events (trials); second column: share of GPU time to failure
sources.note: 39,776 failure events. The paper tags each reason Infrastructure (IF), AI engine (AE) or User (U), often several at once; the mapping here picks one (ours). Its "top-8 cover 88.9%" computes to 87.6%. "programming errors dominating failures and occurring early"; infrastructure failures are rare but "have much longer runtime to failure".

sources.name: Top 5% most resource-intensive tasks
sources.unit: share of task terminations (no counts printed)
sources.note: 56.6% of these tasks succeeded; the 43.4% that did not are shown. Transient faults are "73% of all errors"; a typical 68-minute downtime = 30 min to notice a hang + 9 resubmit + 14 environment + 15 recompute (adds up).

sources.name: One 4,096-GPU job, one month
sources.note: 40 crashes in a month (counts reconstructed from the percentages). Its Table III: one 2,400-GPU job lost 31.19% of its time to failures in June 2023 (diagnosis alone 19.65%), 1.16% by December 2023.

sources.name: Fire-Flyer 2, one year
sources.note: 12,970 Xid events; every percentage reproduces. The paper groups xid 13, 31, 43 and 45 as "software causes"; Xid events are driver messages, many per incident, so shares are of messages.

sources.name: ByteDance training cluster, seven months
sources.note: Shares add to 100.1. "a training task can encounter two faults per day on average".

sources.name: 504 B200, 55 days
sources.cite: From Detection to Recovery (Lablup technical report, arXiv 2605.09370v5), Table 2
sources.note: 17 events in 55 days on 63 nodes: 4.9 per 1,000 node-days (our arithmetic), between Meta's two research clusters.

sources.name: Meta RSC-1 research cluster
sources.cite: Kokolis et al., Revisiting Reliability in Large-Scale ML Research Clusters (HPCA 2025), Figure 3 (arXiv 2410.21680v2)
sources.unit: final state of every job (share of jobs; share of GPU runtime)
sources.note: Hardware failures are 0.2% of jobs but 18.7% of GPU runtime: big jobs are the ones hardware kills. 6.50 failures per 1,000 node-days on RSC-1 and 2.34 on RSC-2. Mapping job states to causes is ours and coarse (a FAILED job can also be a software fault). "Many hardware failures are unattributed, and the most common attributed failures are due to the backend network, the filesystem, and GPUs."

no_table.name: OPT-175B logbook (Meta, 2022)
no_table.what: A free-text on-call diary, no cause table: ECC errors, lost GPUs, CUDA "unspecified launch failure", bad InfiniBand and slow NCCL nodes, hangs, checkpoint downloads that hung, a cloud replacement that returned the same bad machine; "~2 machines go down every day", "40+ restarts" between Nov 17 and Dec 3. The paper: at least 35 manual and an estimated 70+ automatic restarts on 992 A100s in about 2 months.

no_table.name: MegaScale (ByteDance, NSDI 2024)
no_table.what: No cause table: one production run on more than 10,000 GPUs restarted "over 100 times" in several weeks; over 90% of faults detected and recovered automatically; detection plus diagnostics "less than 10 minutes", catch-up "within 15 minutes".

no_table.name: BLOOM 176B (BigScience, 2022)
no_table.what: "1-2 GPU failures occurred each week" on 384 A100s; no table.

no_table.name: Gemini 1.0 (Google, 2023)
no_table.what: No table: SDC "every week or two"; goodput 85% to 97% with in-memory replicas.
